$comment: SPEC §25.4 / §30.4 / §9 — one chat turn, as it crosses the wire. Both transports serve this same shape: `POST /v1/chat/turn` (the §32.11 handoff path) and the §34.6 socket's `captions.final`. One declaration, because a turn that renders one way over HTTP and another over the socket is two chat screens wearing one name.

role.$comment: §25.4's two authors. There is no third — group mechanics are deliberately dropped from the WhatsApp grammar, so there is no shape here that could carry a third party.

safety_level.$comment: §9's L1–L5 ladder, as the client must see it. §22.9 and §29.1: L3+ takes the screen over. The threshold is DECLARED below rather than written as `>= 3` on each side.

source_state.$comment: §34.7's three VerifiedSourceRow states. Served, never inferred client-side: whether two almanacs corroborated a fact is something only §32.2's adjudication knows.

SAFETY_TAKEOVER_FROM_ORDINAL.$comment: §22.9 / §29.1 — 'safety takeover (/support/now, L3+)'. One number, read by the server when it decides and by the client when it renders, so the two can never disagree about what L3+ means.

CITATION_SPANS_ARE_SENTENCES.$comment: §30.4 — the citation marker sits INSIDE the sentence, before the final stop (the rule daily-guidance's composer already follows), and the grounding validator judges a sentence at a time. So the underlined span is the sentence, which is the unit that was actually verified. A narrower span would claim a precision nothing measured.

ChatTrust.$comment: §30.4's three layers, already rendered — the same shape and the same reason as TodayTrust. Fact IDs are absent BY SHAPE: there is no field one could travel in, which is the guarantee TrustSheet's props already give on the component side.

ChatCitation.$comment: §25.4's fact-citation underline. `span_start`/`span_end` index into the turn's `text` (Unicode code points, not UTF-16 units — Devanagari and emoji both make those differ). One citation per verified sentence.

MemoryChipOffer.$comment: §32.4 — a SUGGESTION. Nothing is stored without the explicit chip, so this shape carries no memory id: there is no memory yet. `requires_reconfirmation` is types 7–9's 'always re-confirm wording before save'.

ChatTurn.$comment: One of Tara's turns, after every §9 validator has passed. There is no shape for an unvalidated one, anywhere, in either language — which is what makes 'a fabricated claim never reaches a bubble' a property of the contract rather than a rule someone has to keep.
